cohort: 180 infants born at 34-40 weeks gestation at the Benazir Bhutto Hospital in Rawalpindi, excluding those with congenital defects, surgical intervention, hypoxic ischemic encephalopathy, or prior antibiotic treatment.
finding: S.Aureus (27.86%) and E.Coli (22.14%) were the most common organisms isolated in early-onset neonatal sepsis cases, followed by Staphylococcus epidermidis (15%) and Klebseila (12.86%), with resistance observed to Ampicillin, Cefotaxime, Ceftriaxone, and Ceftazidime.
